headline: University of Pennsylvania researchers report that 13 epilepsy patients could chat with their monitoring device through a phone app, and that doing so helped the system spot seizures better.
score_reason: Peer-reviewed in Nature Medicine, but a small proof of concept with no health outcomes yet.
importance_line: It points to devices that learn from patients, which could help people with epilepsy and other conditions, though it was tested on only 13 patients in a hospital unit.
summary: Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania report in Nature Medicine that 13 epilepsy patients under brain monitoring could ask questions, report symptoms and flag false alarms through a phone app, and that this feedback improved the system's seizure detection; The Washington Post also covered the study. The team says later work will test whether it reduces seizures and hospital visits, so health benefits are not yet shown.
notes: Washington Post page unreachable; used the Penn release (the researchers' own account). Whether outcomes improve is not yet shown.
